subject: Service canonicalization, DNS delegation, and TLS proxying plan for Finora private deployment
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@finora.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@finora.com, security@finora.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service naming and TLS for our VPC/private endpoints

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the discussion this morning. To prepare for our Private deployment cutover we need a short, actionable plan covering:

- Canonical hostnames for tenant-facing endpoints (we currently have multiple temporary CNAMEs).
- DNS delegation model (split-horizon at their resolver vs delegate subzone to our nameservers).
- Cert issuance: who signs CSRs, OCSP responsibilities, and renewal cadence.
- TLS termination options (mutual TLS at edge vs TLS passthrough to backend).

A few constraints from security: Finora requires (1) auditable CSR signing for any certs trusted by their services, (2) OCSP stapling enabled or short-lived certs, and (3) clear ownership of DNS records.

Can your team propose a minimal path that avoids host-level rework on their side and keeps us compliant? We can do an initial 30-agent pilot in their staging VPC next month.

Attachments: none in this message.

Best,
James
Director, Platform Engineering
Finora Payments
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: James Lee <james.lee@finora.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service naming and TLS for our VPC/private endpoints

James — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Jonas, Marissa and Neha to align on the implementation and timeline.

High level proposal (short path + compliance):

1) Canonicalization: create tenant-specific hostnames under a delegated subdomain we control, e.g. finora.tenant.redwood.internal (publicly private via split-horizon). This lets Finora point a single CNAME (api.finora.com) to our canonical alias in their staging and prod without needing per-service changes.

2) DNS Delegation: two supported options — (A) Finora delegates a narrow subzone (tenant.redwood.internal) to our authoritative nameservers (preferred for automation), or (B) Finora maintains split-horizon entries in their resolver and maps the CNAMEs to internal IPs. Option A simplifies cert provisioning and TTL-based rotations.

3) Certificate flow: we will use an ACME-compatible internal broker for short-lived certs (7–14 day TTL) and OCSP stapling enabled at the edge. For air-gapped/on-prem where ACME is blocked, we provide a signed CSR workflow (CSR template attached) and an auditable signing log. For externally visible certs (if any), Finora's PKI team needs to review the CA chain.

4) TLS termination: recommend TLS termination at the Redwood ingress (mutual TLS optional). For customers wanting end-to-end mTLS, we can offer TLS passthrough to their backend with a pinned client cert. For most customers the right balance is termination at the edge with mTLS between edge and backend inside the VPC.

Next steps / Owners:
- Finora: decide on delegation vs split-horizon and provide DNS ACL contact (James) — due 2026-09-21.
- Redwood (Jonas): provide ACME broker endpoint and CSR template; implement ephemeral cert proof-of-concept in staging — due 2026-09-28.
- Redwood (Marissa): run compliance checklist and produce trust matrix for Finora's security review — due 2026-09-24.

Attaching CSR template, trust matrix stub, and our internal runbook for ACME broker.

Attachments:
- csr_template.pem (text/x-pem)
- trust_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
- internal-acme-runbook.md (text/markdown)

If the team is aligned I can schedule a 30-minute tech review with Finora next week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, James Lee <james.lee@finora.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service naming and TLS for our VPC/private endpoints

Laura / James — quick follow-up with the technical tradeoffs my team prefers.

Notes and rationale:
- Delegated subzone: we prefer narrow delegation (tenant.redwood.internal) because it lets us provision TXT records for ACME validation automatically, rotate A/AAAA records without involving Finora's DNS team, and scale across tenants. Delegation requires a short checklist on ACLs and monitoring but pays dividends for automation.

- Hostname canonicalization: avoid SRV for HTTPS endpoints — most clients don't support SRV for TLS. Use canonical hostnames + path-based routing at the edge. For multi-tenant routing, use SNI to map incoming traffic to tenant config. Suggest canonical hostnames follow the pattern <env>.<tenant>.rwd-internal (e.g. stg.finora.rwd-internal).

- Cert model: two modes:
  a) ACME ephemeral certs issued by our internal ACME CA with OCSP stapling at our edge. Renewals handled by the broker; Finora gets an audit log and CSR ID for traceability.
  b) For customers who require their own root, accept signed CSRs and return a chain; we will enforce short TTLs and an automated expiration watch.

- mTLS: for the pilot, terminate TLS at the ingress and use mTLS between our ingress and the service mesh inside the customer's VPC. That minimizes changes to customer-facing clients and preserves end-to-end identity inside the network.

Operational items we need from Finora:
1) DNS delegation record (NS set) or explicit A/CNAME list for split-horizon.
2) Point of contact for PKI approval and an expected lead time for root review.
3) Confirmation on whether they will accept OCSP stapling or require short-lived certs only.

I can spin up the ACME broker POC in our staging cluster by 2026-09-28 and provide a runbook for Finora's ops to test CSR exchange via SFTP if their network policy disallows direct ACME calls.

On the quoting question: OCSP responders and short-lived cert support are covered under the Private add-on in the draft SOW; we'll finalize pricing after the pilot.

—Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Lee <james.lee@finora.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service naming and TLS for our VPC/private endpoints — pilot kickoff and checklist

All — thanks for the proposals. From a compliance and program perspective here's the plan I will own and the immediate checklist we'll run with Finora for the pilot next week: 

Checklist (pilot):
- Finora to provide either NS delegation for tenant.redwood.internal OR a CSV of A/CNAME entries for three staging hosts (due 2026-09-22).
- Redwood to provision ACME broker POC and supply ephemeral certs to staging (2026-09-28).
- Security review: Finora to confirm acceptable CA chain (internal or our broker) and sign off on OCSP stapling (2026-09-24).
- Audit trail: Redwood will export CSR signing logs and provide a signed manifest for any hand-signed CSRs.
- Failover: If delegation is not possible, we will run split-horizon with a documented rollback window (TTL=60s) and test HTTP -> HTTPS redirections.

Deliverables to Finora before pilot:
- trust_matrix.xlsx (attached) — maps responsibilities for DNS, certs, OCSP, and monitoring.
- internal-acme-runbook.md (attached) — steps for ACME validation, CSR exchange fallback, and troubleshooting.
- RFC-style doc summarizing canonical hostnames and SNI mapping (will share draft by 2026-09-23).

I'll schedule the 30-minute tech review once we see delegation confirmation from Finora. If they cannot do delegation, Jonas' SFTP CSR exchange approach will be the fallback.

Marissa Cole
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
